newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt plans to hold budget deficit to 1 pct of GDP.
newsitem.headline: Egypt plans to hold budget deficit to 1 pct of GDP.

text.p: The Egyptian government, in the budget it is preparing for the financial year 1997/8, will cut the budget deficit to one percent of gross domestic product, government newspapers said on Tuesday.
The deficit in the current 1996/7 year, which ends on June 30, was budgeted at 1.5 percent of GDP but ministers say they managed to trim it to 1.1 percent in the first six months.

The newspapers, quoting a briefing at the Ministry of Finance, said total government spending in 1997/8 would rise 10 percent to 85 billion pounds ($25 billion). Spending this year was projected at 77.7 billion.
The newspapers did not give figures for projected revenues or for the absolute size of the deficit.
Finance Ministry officials were not available to confirm the budget figures.
